Summary  
Data source overview: The appendix of an ICLR-22 paper introduces MEME – a test-time adaptation (TTA) method that minimises marginal prediction entropy over multiple augmentations of each individual test image.  The appendix supplies experimental protocol, ablations and detailed results on CIFAR-10-C/-10.1, ImageNet-C/-R/-A showing sizeable accuracy gains versus baselines such as Tent, TTA and single-point Batch-Norm (BN) adaptation.  
EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[87] – The paper gives explicit quantitative evidence for every link in the main causal chain; remaining uncertainty comes from having only the appendix (core motivation paragraphs are not shown).  
Inference strategy justification: Where motivation text is missing, moderate inference (confidence = 2) was used to reconstruct the canonical risk and problem analysis nodes (“Performance degradation … under distribution shift”, “Covariate and corruption shifts …”) which are implicitly addressed by all robustness papers cited.  
Extraction completeness explanation: All reasoning steps that connect the safety-relevant risk to the concrete MEME deployment recommendation are represented.  Two parallel implementation mechanisms (MEME with AugMix, single-point BN adaptation) and both validation blocks are included so the fabric is connected and non-redundant (11 nodes, 9 edges).  
Key limitations: 1) Paper scope is limited to image classification; generalisation to other modalities is not evidenced. 2) Operational deployment experience is absent, so intervention maturity is set to 2 (experimental). 3) We do not model detailed hyper-parameter choices as standalone nodes to avoid over-fragmentation.
